title: Add JSONSchema structured output: strict mode, improved errors, OpenAI compatibility
author: Maya Chen
commits: feat(api): add response_format=json_schema support and validation pipeline
fix(runtime): streaming validator -> buffer/emit partial chunk validation to avoid blocking
docs: update structured output docs and OpenAI compatibility examples
description: Context: Product request to provide first-class JSONSchema structured output support and a strict validation mode that's compatible with OpenAI style response_format semantics. This PR implements response_format=json_schema and response_format: {type: "json_schema", schema: <JSONSchema>, strict: true|false} at the API surface, adds server-side schema validation with clear error codes, updates streaming validator behavior to avoid blocking long-running streams, and adds OpenAI compatibility helpers in the SDKs. Motivation: customers need deterministic structured outputs for downstream parsing and to catch regressions early. Summary: - API: add response_format param parsing and OpenAI-compat mappings. - Validation: implement JSONSchema v2020-12 compatible validator, with an optional strict mode that rejects outputs that do not conform (returns structured error). - Streaming: non-blocking partial validation (validate chunks/records as they complete) and fallbacks for partially-invalid streams to avoid head-of-line blocking. - Errors: introduce structured error payloads and error codes (STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION, STRICT_MODE_VIOLATION, VALIDATION_TIMEOUT) to make client handling deterministic. - SDKs: add openai_compat helpers and example usage; map existing openai response_format fields to Redwood semantics. - Docs/examples/tests: add API docs, examples for strict and permissive modes, and unit/e2e benches. Checklist: - [x] API parsing and surface implemented - [x] Server-side validator + schema registry hooks - [x] Streaming validator changes (non-blocking emit) - [x] SDK changes (Python/TS) + examples - [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests added - [x] Benchmarks and perf regression check - [x] Docs updated Rollout/compat: default behavior is permissive (strict=false) behind feature flag redwood.features.structured_output. Enable strict mode only when explicitly requested by API user. For OpenAI compatibility we map the OpenAI style response_format and function/tool-calling outputs into our validator and add example migration notes in docs. Testing: added unit tests for schema validation, fuzz tests for edge-case schemas, e2e tests for streaming strict mode, and benchmarks to ensure <5% p50 latency regression in common workloads. Follow-ups: add schema caching across requests, admin tooling for schema lifecycle, telemetry for strict-mode rejections.
review_comments: Ravi: Please add explicit error codes and a stable schema error shape for clients to switch on — done and added pkg/errors/structured_errors.go
Elena: Concern about streaming head-of-line blocking — addressed by implementing chunked validation and early emit of validated fragments
Samir: Verify perf impact on p50/p95; re-run benches after optimization — benches show <5% p50 regression, p95 within SLOs

release_notes: Add JSONSchema structured output support and strict validation mode. New structured error codes for schema violations. Default behavior remains permissive; strict mode opt-in. SDKs updated for OpenAI compatibility.
